questions.a: The Response Gap is the time between a guest expressing dissatisfaction and your brand responding. The longer it runs, the more likely the guest is to assume nothing will change and move to a competitor. Momos's analysis of 30,000+ locations links slow responses to churn at underperforming stores.

questions.q: How fast should a restaurant respond to guest feedback?
questions.a: Aim to acknowledge feedback within minutes, and certainly within a day. According to Sprout Social, most consumers expect brands to reply within 24 hours on social media, and faster is better. A quick acknowledgment shows accountability and keeps a negative impression from spreading.

questions.q: Why do slow responses hurt underperforming stores more?
questions.a: Strong stores have enough goodwill to absorb an occasional mistake, while struggling stores don't. When a laggard store stays silent, guests read it as a sign the store is poorly run and take their business elsewhere. That speeds up the decline the store is already in.

questions.q: Does responding to reviews really affect revenue?
questions.a: Responsiveness shapes whether guests trust you enough to come back. BrightLocal research cited in the post found that consumers are more likely to use a business that responds to reviews. When brands close the Response Gap, engagement improves, issues decline and stores stabilize.

questions.q: How can managers respond faster without burning out?
questions.a: Treat response time like any other operational metric and support it with automation. Fast acknowledgments, automatic detection of recurring issues and clear, prioritized alerts on mobile make the work lighter. The goal is more clarity and a simpler workflow for managers, without adding to their workload.
